conventions.offset: Addresses are the frame addresses. The apps store a RELATIVE OFFSET from the space's base_address (data 36000, settings 36500); address = base + offset and wire_offset is 0. The PV -1 correction does NOT apply here.
conventions.identity: A register is identified by (device, space, address). EPM and EPM-AX share both base addresses but not their meanings — offsets 9, 10 and 13 name different settings on each device, which is why the two devices are separate files.
conventions.width: Width comes from the data-type column. U32/S32 are two consecutive registers, low word first.
conventions.word_order: 32-bit registers are LITTLE-endian (low word first) — the opposite of PV. Stated in each register's own description and confirmed against a live 3-phase capture on 2026-08-07.
conventions.precedence: overrides > app agreement > document (newest first). Both apps agree on every address, so conflicts here are app-vs-document or between the two apps' enum labels.

register_spaces.note: EPM operational information from 36000. Printed address is the frame address — no offset.

rule.title: EPM Power Total
rule.summary: Total power measured at the grid connection point, across all three phases. Negative means exporting to the grid.
rule.gotcha: This is a 32-bit register and it is LITTLE-endian — low word first, the opposite of every PV register. Decoding it big-endian does not fail loudly; it returns a plausible-looking number in the hundreds of thousands of kW. A live 3-phase site showed exactly that before the fix.
rule.check: The total must equal the sum of the three phase registers (36006, 36007, 36008), which are plain 16-bit and never affected by word order. If it does not, the word order is wrong.
sources: V19 36009 description — 'Note: Little Endian Low first, High Latter'

registers.note: Deliberately left WITHOUT units, and this is a decision, not a gap. 36011 is what the inverters report about THEMSELVES over the comms bus — their own real watts. It never passes through the EPM's CT clamps, so it must NOT be multiplied by CT or PT; doing so would inflate a already-correct figure by the CT ratio. The extension's transformer rule is units-driven, so an empty `units` string is exactly what keeps it unscaled. The app's own description map records kW, which is right for DISPLAY but must not be copied here, because here it would turn the multiply on. Tanner, 2026-08-21: 'No — inverters report their own real watts.'

registers.note: Serial number as TEXT, not a number, and 16 registers long. The extension maps `sn` as 16 consecutive registers from offset 30; Tauri maps it as a single register, which would show only the first two characters. The documents print 36030-36049 as one 'Reserve' span and never name the field, so neither app is confirmed by the document — but a 1-register serial number cannot be right, and the extension's tables were the ones that proved correct about PV. Same reasoning as the failSafe/controlProtocol calls (Tanner, 2026-08-21). If a live read shows anything other than readable text here, remove this override.

rule.title: CT Ratio
rule.summary: Tells the EPM how big the current transformers (the clamps around the cable that measure current) are.
rule.write_explain: Write the ratio directly. A 200:1 CT is written as 200.
rule.gotcha: Every power and current reading is multiplied by this number. Getting it wrong scales the whole site's readings, and the EPM will limit at the wrong point — but nothing reports an error, because the readings still look like plausible numbers.

rule.summary: How much power is allowed to flow back to the grid before the EPM starts limiting the inverters.
rule.write_explain: Write the value directly. Zero means no export is allowed at all.
rule.gotcha: The documents disagree on this register's sign — some print it U16 and some S16. A negative value only means anything if the sign is real, so a site that needs a negative backflow setting must be checked against the live reading rather than trusted from the map.

rule.summary: Picks how the EPM limits export.
rule.write_explain: Write the mode number directly. One mode runs at a time — this is a selector, not a set of flags.

rule.write_explain: 0 is OFF, 1 is ON. Default is OFF.
rule.gotcha: EPM-AX reuses this address for a five-value FailSafe mode, and the two apps do not agree on what those five values mean. The simple 0/1 documented here is the EPM meaning only.
